content.name: Mónika Papp
openTo: contract research on document matching and data reconciliation
consulting on multilingual NLP system design

bio.text: Mónika Papp completed her undergraduate and master's studies in Mathematics and Computer Science at the University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Sciences, graduating in 2005 and 2007 respectively. She earned her PhD in 2013 with a dissertation on cross-lingual sentence alignment in multilingual legal corpora. After a postdoctoral stay at the University of Ljubljana (2014–2015), she returned to Novi Sad as a Research Associate and was promoted to Senior Research Associate in 2020. Her group focuses on multilingual natural language processing, with particular emphasis on transformer-based semantic similarity, named-entity alignment, and structured document reconciliation across typologically diverse languages. She teaches courses in computational linguistics and machine learning for text data. The group uses GPU-equipped workstations and accesses HPC resources through the Institute of Mathematics of the Serbian Academy of Sciences.

industryExperience.text: Papp carried out a six-month applied research engagement with a regional insurance company (2018–2019) focused on automated cross-lingual matching of damage-claim documents submitted in Serbian and Hungarian. The engagement resulted in a prototype system deployed internally by the company.

notes.text: Papp is currently at full teaching load and can take on new projects only from late 2025 onward. She has a strong preference for projects with a clearly defined applied component and real multilingual document data rather than purely benchmark-oriented work.

works.title: Sentence-Level Alignment in Multilingual Legal Texts Using Lexical Overlap and Cognate Features

body.text: This paper addresses the problem of sentence alignment in parallel legal corpora involving Hungarian, Serbian, and English. We constructed a manually annotated corpus of 4,200 sentence pairs extracted from EU directive translations and national legislative texts. Alignment was performed using a combination of lexical overlap scores, cognate detection based on edit distance, and length-ratio heuristics. We compared four alignment strategies—Gale-Church length-based, Hunalign, a simple TF-IDF cosine method, and a rule-augmented hybrid—on three language pairs. The hybrid approach achieved F1 scores of 0.87, 0.83, and 0.79 for EN–SR, EN–HU, and HU–SR pairs respectively, outperforming all baselines. Error analysis revealed that cross-linguistic terminological divergence and inconsistent paragraph segmentation in source documents were the dominant failure modes. The annotated corpus and alignment scripts are released under a CC-BY licence.

works.title: A Comparative Study of Bilingual Lexicon Induction Methods for Serbian–Hungarian Word Pairs in Technical Domains

body.text: Bilingual lexicon induction (BLI) without parallel corpora is particularly challenging for morphologically rich, closely situated language pairs. This study evaluates four BLI approaches—cross-lingual word embedding projection, iterative Procrustes alignment, VecMap, and a graph-based method—on Serbian–Hungarian word pairs sampled from three technical domains: civil engineering, agriculture, and information technology. Evaluation dictionaries containing 2,100 pairs per domain were assembled from terminological databases and validated by domain experts. Results show that iterative Procrustes alignment achieves the highest precision@1 (42.3%) on the IT domain, while graph-based methods perform better on agriculture (38.7% precision@1), where morphological regularity is lower. All methods degrade substantially on out-of-vocabulary compound terms. We release the three domain dictionaries and pre-trained fastText vectors fine-tuned on a 600 M token Serbian–Hungarian corpus.

works.title: Cross-Lingual Named-Entity Linking Between Serbian and English News Corpora Using Wikipedia Anchors

body.text: Named-entity linking (NEL) across languages is complicated by transliteration variation, partial name translations, and entity ambiguity. We describe a system that links named entities in Serbian news articles to English Wikipedia entries using a combination of anchor text statistics, Wikidata cross-reference mappings, and string similarity features. We evaluated on a manually annotated dataset of 3,800 entity mentions drawn from four Serbian news portals, covering persons, organisations, and locations. The proposed system achieved a linking accuracy of 74.2% on persons and 68.9% on organisations, compared to 61.4% and 55.7% for a transliteration-only baseline. We analyse error categories and find that local public figures with sparse Wikipedia coverage account for roughly 40% of failures. The annotated mention dataset is made publicly available.

works.title: Reconciling Duplicate Patient Records Across Hospital Systems: A Cross-Lingual Entity Matching Approach

body.text: Electronic health record systems in multilingual regions often store patient and diagnostic data in different languages, leading to duplicate and conflicting records. This chapter presents a framework for cross-lingual entity matching of patient records in Serbian and Hungarian administrative data, using a combination of phonetic normalisation, transliteration, and fuzzy attribute matching. A prototype was developed and tested on a synthetic dataset of 10,000 record pairs generated from anonymised templates provided by a regional hospital administration. We define five match categories ranging from definite match to definite non-match and report precision of 0.91 and recall of 0.86 for the definite match category. The chapter discusses practical barriers including inconsistent date formats, name order conventions, and missing-field patterns common in legacy systems.

works.title: Evaluating Multilingual Sentence Encoders on a Diverse Cross-Lingual Semantic Textual Similarity Benchmark for South Slavic Languages

body.text: Publicly available semantic textual similarity (STS) benchmarks rarely include South Slavic languages, making it difficult to evaluate multilingual encoder models in this region. We construct STS-SlaVoSe, a benchmark of 5,400 sentence pairs in Serbian, Croatian, Slovenian, and Bosnian, covering six domains: news, legal texts, social media, scientific abstracts, product descriptions, and conversational transcripts. Each pair was annotated by three annotators on a 0–5 scale; inter-annotator Pearson correlation averaged 0.83. We evaluate eight publicly available multilingual sentence encoders including mBERT, XLM-R, LaBSE, and four smaller distilled variants. LaBSE achieves the highest average Pearson correlation (0.79) across all language–domain combinations, though performance varies markedly by domain: legal text pairs yield the lowest scores (0.61) across all models. We release the full benchmark under CC-BY-SA.

works.title: Fine-Tuning Multilingual Transformers for Cross-Lingual Document Matching in Public Procurement

body.text: Public procurement databases in the Western Balkans are maintained in multiple national languages, making cross-border tender matching difficult without manual translation. We investigate whether fine-tuned multilingual transformer models can identify semantically equivalent tender notices across Serbian, Croatian, and Macedonian without explicit translation. Using a dataset of 12,400 tender notice pairs (6,200 positive, 6,200 negative) derived from the Open Tenders Balkans portal, we fine-tune XLM-R and mBERT with a siamese network objective and compare against a TF-IDF baseline and a machine-translation-then-monolingual-SBERT pipeline. The fine-tuned XLM-R siamese model achieves an average precision of 0.88 on the held-out test set, compared to 0.73 for TF-IDF and 0.85 for the translation pipeline, while running approximately 3.4× faster at inference time. We discuss domain-specific vocabulary challenges and release fine-tuning code.

works.title: Structured Table Reconciliation Across Multilingual Financial Reports Using Column-Header Alignment and Cell-Level Semantic Similarity

body.text: Annual financial reports published by companies operating across multiple Central and Eastern European jurisdictions often contain the same underlying data structured in tables with headers in different languages and with variable column ordering. This paper presents a pipeline for aligning and reconciling such tables automatically. Column headers are aligned using cross-lingual sentence embeddings (LaBSE and XLM-R) combined with a type-inference module that classifies cells as numeric, date, currency, or free text. Cell-level reconciliation uses a combination of normalised numeric comparison and semantic similarity for textual cells. We evaluate on a corpus of 840 paired tables from 210 annual reports covering Serbian, Hungarian, and Romanian. Column alignment achieves an F1 of 0.92; full-row reconciliation with conflict detection reaches a precision of 0.87. The pipeline reduces manual review time by an estimated 65% in a controlled user study with eight financial analysts.

works.title: A Modular Framework for Cross-Lingual Reconciliation of Structured Administrative Documents: Architecture and Case Studies

body.text: Administrative bodies in multilingual regions routinely exchange structured documents—forms, certificates, registrations—whose fields are defined by different national schema vocabularies. This paper describes DocAlign-ML, a modular software framework that combines schema-level field mapping, cross-lingual semantic similarity scoring, and value normalisation to reconcile such documents automatically. The framework consists of four interchangeable modules: a field-label encoder based on fine-tuned XLM-R, a type-aware value normaliser, a conflict resolver, and an explainability layer that generates natural-language justifications for each mapping decision. We present three case studies: business registration documents in Serbian and Romanian, land cadastre records in Serbian and Hungarian, and birth certificate data in Serbian and German. Average field-mapping accuracy across the three cases is 0.89. The framework is implemented in Python and the core components are released as open-source libraries.

works.title: Contrastive Fine-Tuning of Sentence Encoders on Small Domain-Specific Parallel Corpora: A Study on Legal and Medical Subdomains

body.text: Large multilingual sentence encoders trained on general web data often perform poorly on specialised domains where vocabulary and sentence structure differ substantially from general text. We investigate the effectiveness of contrastive fine-tuning—using in-domain positive pairs and hard negatives mined from the same corpus—when the available domain-specific parallel corpus is small (2,000–8,000 sentence pairs). Experiments cover two subdomains (legal and medical) and three language pairs (EN–SR, EN–HU, EN–RO). We compare full fine-tuning, adapter-based fine-tuning, and prompt-based fine-tuning on top of LaBSE and XLM-R-large. Adapter-based fine-tuning with hard-negative mining matches or exceeds full fine-tuning on all six subdomain–language-pair combinations while using 7% of the trainable parameters. Performance gains are most pronounced on the medical subdomain (average Pearson correlation improvement of +0.11 over the base model). We provide a systematic analysis of hard-negative quality and its impact on final performance.

works.title: Evaluating Hallucination and Semantic Drift in Cross-Lingual Summaries Generated by Instruction-Tuned LLMs for Structured Documents

body.text: Instruction-tuned large language models are increasingly used to generate cross-lingual summaries of structured documents such as regulatory filings and procurement notices. However, it remains unclear how reliably these models preserve factual content and named-entity references when summarising across language pairs. We design an evaluation protocol using 1,200 structured document pairs in four language pairs (EN–SR, EN–HU, SR–RO, HU–RO) and three document types: regulatory filings, procurement notices, and scientific project abstracts. Three instruction-tuned models are evaluated: a 7B and a 13B open-weight model, and a proprietary API model. We measure hallucination rate (entity-level and numerical), semantic similarity between source and summary (using cross-lingual STS), and named-entity recall. The 13B open-weight model hallucinates named entities in 18.4% of generated summaries; the proprietary model reduces this to 9.1% but still introduces numeric errors in 6.7% of cases. We release the evaluation protocol, annotation guidelines, and test set.

works.title: Stochastic Fluid Models for Burst-Tolerant Auto-Scaling in Container Orchestration Platforms

body.text: Container orchestration systems such as those based on declarative scheduling can scale replica counts in response to observed CPU utilisation, but default horizontal scaling policies do not account for the statistical structure of workload bursts. This paper adapts the stochastic fluid queue framework to model container-level resource consumption when arrivals follow a Markov-modulated process with two burst modes. The fluid level represents the accumulated processing backlog. Buffer overflow probabilities and expected drain times are derived in closed form using spectral decomposition of the generator matrix. The model is parameterised from a 72-hour trace of HTTP request arrivals to a microservices application running on an in-house three-node cluster. Predicted overflow probabilities match observed SLA breach rates with a mean absolute error of 0.008 across 15 experimental conditions. The paper proposes a scaling trigger rule based on the fluid model's overflow threshold and shows it reduces SLA violations by 31 percent compared to a CPU-only threshold rule in a controlled replay experiment.

works.title: Stochastic Optimisation of Checkpointing Intervals for Fault-Tolerant Scientific Workflows on Heterogeneous Clouds

body.text: Long-running scientific workflow tasks benefit from periodic checkpointing to limit recomputation after node failures, but frequent checkpointing imposes I/O overhead. This paper models the workflow execution as a renewal reward process in which the checkpoint interval T is the decision variable, task failure rate λ follows an inhomogeneous Poisson process estimated from node-failure logs, and I/O overhead is a linear function of checkpoint size. The expected waste ratio—proportion of CPU time spent on recomputation and checkpointing—is derived analytically and minimised with respect to T for a given λ(t) profile. A closed-form approximately-optimal interval is obtained under the assumption that λ(t) is piecewise constant. The formula is validated on a simulation of a 128-node heterogeneous cluster over 500 simulated workflow executions. Optimal intervals range from 12 to 47 minutes depending on failure rate and checkpoint size, reducing waste by 28–36 percent compared to a fixed 30-minute interval baseline.

works.title: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Queue Management in Edge-Cloud Continuum Deployments

body.text: Edge nodes in a continuum deployment have limited queuing capacity and must decide whether to process requests locally or offload them to a central cloud tier. This paper formulates the per-edge offloading decision as a Markov decision process solved approximately by a tabular Q-learning agent. The state is a discretised pair of local queue length and observed round-trip latency to the cloud. Reward is the negative of per-request sojourn time. The agent is trained in a simulated environment parameterised from latency and arrival-rate measurements at two edge nodes of a pilot deployment at the NTP Novi Sad testbed during a three-week collection period. After convergence (approximately 800,000 simulated steps), the learned policy reduces mean sojourn time by 14 percent and 99th-percentile sojourn time by 23 percent compared to a static threshold offloading rule. Robustness to distributional shift is tested by applying the policy under a workload with 30 percent higher arrival rate; degradation is modest, with mean sojourn time increasing by 9 percent over the trained-condition optimum.

works.title: A Branch-and-Bound Approach to the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Hard Time Windows

body.text: This paper addresses the capacitated vehicle routing problem with hard time windows (CVRPTW) using a branch-and-bound algorithm enhanced by a set of dominance rules derived from Lagrangian relaxation. The test instances are drawn from the Solomon benchmark suite as well as a locally generated dataset of 40 instances representing urban delivery scenarios in a mid-size city network with 80–150 customer nodes. The branching strategy prioritises fractional arc variables with highest reduced cost, and lower bounds are tightened using a column-generation subproblem solved by a shortest-path procedure on an auxiliary time-expanded graph. Computational experiments show that the proposed algorithm closes 87% of Solomon's 100-customer instances within a two-hour time limit on a standard quad-core workstation, reducing the average optimality gap to 1.3% compared to 4.7% for a standard LP-relaxation baseline. The approach scales poorly beyond 200 nodes but provides provably optimal or near-optimal solutions for medium-scale instances relevant to last-mile logistics.

works.title: Benchmarking Rolling-Horizon Decomposition Variants for Multi-Modal Urban Freight Scheduling

body.text: Urban freight consolidation centres aim to coordinate deliveries across multiple vehicle types—vans, cargo bikes, and small electric vehicles—within a shared urban zone. This paper adapts rolling-horizon decomposition to a multi-modal dynamic pickup-and-delivery problem and benchmarks four variants differing in window length (60 vs. 120 minutes), overlap policy (fixed vs. adaptive), and sub-problem solver (MILP vs. ALNS). Benchmark instances were constructed from synthetic demand profiles calibrated to freight movement data from two Central European cities. The adaptive-overlap variant with ALNS sub-problem solver achieved the best average performance across 300 instances: 5.3% above the static-day lower bound at a median solve time of 28 seconds per rolling step. Fixed-window MILP was competitive only on low-density instances. The paper provides a parameter-selection guide and open-source instance generator as supplementary materials.

works.title: Pretraga u realnom vremenu nad tokom vesti na srpskom jeziku s mešovitim pismom

body.text: Sistemi za pretragu u realnom vremenu nad tokovima vesti zahtevaju inkrementalno ažuriranje indeksa s niskim kašnjenjem. Kada tok vesti dolazi iz više izvora koji koriste različita pisma, inkrementalni indekser mora da normalizuje pismo svake pristigle stavke pre umetanja. Ovaj rad opisuje arhitekturu sistema koji obrađuje do 1 200 novinskih članaka u minuti, sa prosečnim kašnjenjem indeksiranja od 340 ms na jednom serverskom čvoru s 16 jezgara. Normalizacija pisma i fonemska kanonizacija implementirane su kao paraleln cevovod koji dodaje manje od 15% vremenske cene u odnosu na sistem bez normalizacije. Evaluacija preciznosti pretrage sprovedena je na simuliranom toku od 2,1 miliona članaka prikupljenih tokom 30 dana. Sistem je prilagodljiv i može se horizontalno skalirati dodavanjem čvorova za normalizaciju nezavisno od čvorova za indeksiranje.

works.title: Wiener chaos solutions for a linear elasticity system with spatially random Young's modulus

body.text: We study a system of linear elasticity equations in three spatial dimensions in which Young's modulus is represented as a finite Wiener chaos expansion of order 2, supported by experimental data from tensile tests on polymer composite samples. The random field is characterised by a mean of 3.1 GPa and a coefficient of variation of 18 percent, consistent with measurements reported in the mechanical engineering literature for glass-fibre-reinforced polymers. The Wiener chaos propagator equations form a coupled triangular system of deterministic elliptic boundary value problems, which we solve using a preconditioned conjugate gradient method on a tetrahedral mesh with 84,000 degrees of freedom. We track the evolution of the displacement variance and the von Mises stress distribution across the stochastic domain. The propagator-based approach is compared against a 5,000-sample Monte Carlo reference: the mean displacement field agrees to within 0.4 percent in the L2 norm, while the standard deviation of the von Mises stress is recovered to within 2.1 percent. The method scales linearly in the number of chaos coefficients for orders up to 3.

works.title: Interval Methods for Rigorous Sensitivity Analysis of ODE Solutions with Respect to Initial Conditions

body.text: Sensitivity equations—the variational equations for the derivative of an ODE solution with respect to initial conditions—can be solved simultaneously with the state equations to provide bounds on solution sensitivity. This paper formulates and analyses an interval approach to simultaneous integration of state and first-order sensitivity equations for general non-stiff systems. The extended system doubles the dimension; the paper characterises how wrapping-effect growth scales with dimension and proposes a block-coordinate transformation to mitigate it. Six test cases are used, including the Lorenz system at moderate parameter values. Rigorous sensitivity bounds are compared with finite-difference approximations, and the cases in which interval sensitivity bounds are informative versus overly conservative are characterised. The study also provides a worked example of using sensitivity enclosures to certify local exponential stability of an equilibrium.

works.title: Rigorous Enclosures for Linear ODE Systems with Uncertain Coefficients via Müller's Theorem

body.text: Linear ODE systems whose coefficient matrices are only known to lie within an interval matrix arise naturally in circuit simulation, structural dynamics, and control. This paper applies Müller's monotonicity theorem to derive analytic bounds on the solution set and compares these bounds with those produced by direct interval Taylor integration. For coefficient matrices with interval radius up to 5% of the spectral norm, Müller bounds are tighter than Taylor-model enclosures by a median factor of 2.3 across 18 test cases drawn from circuit simulation netlists. For larger uncertainties the comparison reverses. A hybrid algorithm that selects the tighter enclosure automatically is implemented and tested. The paper also provides a formal characterisation of the subclass of interval matrices for which Müller bounds are guaranteed to be non-explosive over unbounded time intervals.

works.title: Multilingual Document Reconciliation for Cross-Border Administrative Interoperability in the Western Balkans

body.text: MULTIREC addresses the practical problem of reconciling structured administrative documents exchanged between Serbian public institutions and their counterparts in Hungary and Romania, where records are maintained in different languages and schema vocabularies. The project builds on transformer-based cross-lingual semantic similarity to develop automated field-mapping and value-reconciliation tools. Activities include corpus construction (legal, cadastral, and civil registration document pairs), development and evaluation of the DocAlign-ML framework, and a pilot deployment in cooperation with a regional administrative body. The project involves four partners across three countries and has produced six peer-reviewed publications, two open-source software libraries, and training materials for public-sector data managers.

works.title: NLP Tools for Multilingual e-Government Document Exchange in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region

body.text: This Interreg project targets the digitisation and linguistic harmonisation of administrative document workflows in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border area, where a large Hungarian-speaking minority creates demand for bilingual public services. The University of Novi Sad team leads the NLP tools development work package, which covers named-entity alignment, form-field translation, and automated consistency checking for bilingual document pairs. The project partners include municipalities, a regional chamber of commerce, and two universities. Deliverables include a web-based bilingual document assistant, a shared terminological database covering civil administration and land registry domains, and a report on user acceptance among public servants.
